title: Supreme Court Allows White House Ballroom Construction to Proceed; Roberts Dissents
detail: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 on Monday, August 31, 2026, granting the Trump administration's emergency request to let construction continue indefinitely on Trump's roughly $400 million White House ballroom, built on the site of the demolished East Wing. The unsigned majority order found the National Trust for Historic Preservation, which brought the underlying suit, likely lacks legal standing to challenge the project, and did not rule on whether Trump has authority to build without congressional approval. Chief Justice John Roberts joined the court's three liberal justices in dissent, writing that the construction 'is likely unlawful' because federal law bars erecting any building or structure on federal reservations, parks, or public grounds in Washington, D.C. without express congressional authorization.

media.caption: Workers continue construction of the helipad and ballroom on the South Lawn of the White House

title: VP Vance Headlines MAGA Inc. Rally in Sterling Heights, Michigan Ahead of Midterms
detail: Vice President JD Vance headlined a Republican campaign kickoff rally Monday, August 31, 2026 at a manufacturing facility in Sterling Heights, Michigan, hosted by the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc., which holds more than $400 million in cash for the 2026 midterm cycle. The event — Vance's first appearance alongside Michigan's full statewide GOP ticket — featured gubernatorial nominee Rep. John James, Senate nominee Mike Rogers, 10th District nominee Mike Bouchard Jr., Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, FTC Chair Andrew Ferguson, Rep. Lisa McClain, and Michigan House Speaker Matt Hall. Sterling Heights sits in Macomb County, a working-class Detroit-suburb bellwether Republicans are targeting to defend their congressional majority in November.
